schedule.work: Max hangs, then 60–75 min of V9–V10 limit problems
Weighted pull-ups, front lever holds, push-ups or dips, band external rotations, shoulder mobility
Optional ankle and hip mobility, about 15 min
Max hangs, then 60 min on Kilter, Moon or Tension board
Optional 45 min at V5–V7, antagonists, full mobility routine

Max hangs.rx: 20mm edge, half crimp, 10 sec hangs, 3 min rest, a load you could hold about 13 sec (3 sec left)

Limit bouldering.rx: 60–75 min on V9–V10, full rest between attempts

Board session.rx: 60 min of powerful, reachy moves and deadpoints

Projecting.rx: V9–V10, target weaknesses: reachy moves, heel hooks, high feet

Weighted pull-ups.rx: 4 × 3–5 at about RPE 8 (2 reps left), 3–5 min rest

Shoulder mobility routine.rx: Pass-throughs, wall slides, open-book rotations, doorway pec stretch

Ankle and hip mobility.rx: Knee-to-wall, ankle circles, frog stretch 60 sec, 90/90 switches × 10

warmup: Ankle circles, scap pull-ups, band external rotations, then easy climbing up to V6–V7.

method.title: Effort ratings
method.rule: Rate effort as reps (or seconds) left in the tank: RPE 10 = nothing left, 9 = 1 rep, 8 = 2 reps, 7 = 3 reps. Rate the last set, right after it.

method.title: Adjusting to how it felt beats a fixed plan
method.rule: Next loads are set from how the last session went, not from a fixed percentage schedule.
method.evidence: Two meta-analyses: at least as good as fixed loading, maybe slightly better

method.title: Max hangs dose
method.rule: 10 sec hangs on an 18–20mm edge, half crimp, with about 3 sec left, 3 min rest, twice a week. Sets build 3 → 4 → 5 → 5 through each block, then reset.
method.evidence: Several small RCTs and one meta-analysis

method.title: Max hangs: next load
method.rule: 5+ sec left on the last hang: add about 2% of total load (body + added weight). 2–4 sec left: hold. 1 sec or less, or a missed hang: drop about 4%.
method.evidence: Borrowed from a lifting RCT; not yet tested on hangboards

method.title: Weighted pull-ups: next load
method.rule: Aim for RPE 8. Each half point below 7.5 adds about 2%, each half point above 8.5 takes off about 2%, each missed rep takes off about 4%. Pull-ups stay secondary to fingers.
method.evidence: One lifting RCT; no climbing trial of pull-up progression

method.title: No need to train to failure
method.rule: Strength gains are similar across a wide range of reps left, and 2–3 hard sets are enough for strength.

method.title: Planned deload every 5th week
method.rule: Keep training on the same days, but cut volume and effort: 2 lighter hang sets (about 5% lighter), 2 lighter pull-up sets (about 10% lighter), shorter climbing. Not a week off.
method.evidence: Coach consensus and surveys; one RCT found a full week off cost strength

method.title: Early deload when the signs say so
method.rule: Suggest deloading now if: the planned load is missed in 2 sessions in a row, the morning check-in is low 3 days running, or the weekly check shows a substantial finger, elbow or shoulder problem.
method.evidence: Consensus; an unexplained drop in performance is the core sign of overreaching. The thresholds are a judgement call.

method.title: Morning check-in
method.rule: Sleep, energy, soreness, stress and mood (1–5), plus finger pain (0–10). Compared with your own recent average, not a fixed norm.
method.evidence: Systematic review: self-reported measures track training better than objective ones; single items are noisy

method.title: Session load
method.rule: Log session effort (0–10) × minutes. It undercounts finger stress, so hang sets are tracked separately. No acute:chronic workload ratio.
method.evidence: Validated method; ACWR has been shown not to predict injury

method.title: Pain rules
method.rule: Finger pain up to 2/10 during training is fine if it's settled by the next morning. 3–5: no load increases, and skip hangs if it's still there in the morning. 6+, a pop, swelling or the tendon lifting off the bone: stop finger loading and get it scanned.
method.evidence: Pain-monitoring RCT in Achilles tendons (which allows up to 5/10; this is stricter for pulleys) plus expert consensus on pulley injuries

method.title: Retesting
method.rule: Test fresh, on the first days after each deload (every 5 weeks). A change under 6% is within test noise; over 9% is very likely real. When it's real, training loads rescale by the same ratio.

method.title: Grade targets are a reference only
method.rule: No peer-reviewed study gives finger strength for V9 vs V10. Strength explains only part of grade, so the page tracks your own trend.

method.title: Noticing on limit days
method.rule: After limit, board and project sessions, note the crux that stopped you, why (grip, body position, power, fear, beta), and one thing to change next time. Film the crux. The page shows your note at the start of the next one.
method.evidence: Coach consensus; deliberate practice explains some of performance; watching your own good attempts helps short-term; the external-focus effect mostly disappears after correcting for bias

changes: Max hangs: 6 hangs every session → 3–5 sets building through each block, the dose the trials used.
Deload weeks: drop hangboard and weighted pull-ups → keep them, lighter and fewer sets.
Retests: any time in weeks 6–8 → the first days after each deload, when you're fresh.
V10 targets: shown as a rough community reference, since there's no peer-reviewed norm.
